title: DC-area forecast: Heat to intensify through midweek as storm chances build
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Evening temperatures fall back through the 80s and humidity remains high. Overnight lows near 70 to the mid-70s.

What’s next? Uncomfortably hot and humid Tuesday through Thursday, with heat indexes probably peaking near to above 100, although the Wednesday forecast is less certain. Storm chances increase Wednesday and especially Thursday.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: Party to mostly cloudy and humid, with lows near 70 in our cooler areas and the mid-70s downtown. Confidence: Medium-High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Tuesday): The first day of meteorological fall feels far from it. Under partly sunny skies, highs climb to 93 to 98, with heat indexes of 100 to 105 factoring in the humidity (dew points near 70). Some record highs could be challenged. An isolated shower or storm remains possible. Light breezes are from the west. Confidence: Medium-High

Tomorrow night: An unseasonably warm September night. Most spots see lows in the low to mid-70s, but temperatures may struggle to drop below 80 near downtown. Skies are partly cloudy, with little wind to speak of. Confidence: Medium-High

Help sustain an independent Capital Weather. Choose from free and paid ways to support us. Learn more at capitalweather.com/support-us

A look ahead

It remains partly sunny, hot, and humid Wednesday and Thursday. The Wednesday forecast is complicated by an uncertain chance for more clouds and a slightly cooler breeze from the east, which for now means highs anywhere from the upper 80s to mid-90s. Thursday seems more confidently hotter with highs at least in the mid-90s, perhaps flirting with record heat for the day, and heat indexes reaching near to above 100. Both days bring a chance of late-day showers and storms, especially Thursday, when some storms could be severe. Nights remain quite muggy, with lows ranging through the 70s. Confidence: Medium-High

Friday is the transition day between the excessive heat of the previous few days and the more refreshing air on the way. Some heat and mugginess may linger, and showers and storms could pop up, especially south and southeast of DC. Skies are partly sunny, with highs near 90. Drier air should filter in at night. Confidence: Medium

The Labor Day weekend is looking rather promising. High temperatures slip into the low 80s, and humidity also declines, with dew points dipping into the 50s. With high pressure building in, the weather looks partly to mostly sunny and generally dry. If Friday's front slows down and lingers in the Mid-Atlantic into Saturday, we could keep a slight chance of a shower or storm in the forecast. Confidence: Medium

DC weather history for August 31

A violent 1940 thunderstorm brought record rainfall and led to a tragic plane crash in Northern Virginia, then the deadliest in U.S. commercial aviation history.

Today’s daily digit — 3/10: Meteorological summer is ending while temperatures and humidity are headed in the wrong direction: upward. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.
